we_ve_all_been_targeted_with_one_fraudul: We've all been targeted with one fraudulent scheme or another at some point in our adult lives. Now, there is a very realistic-looking scam that falsely claims to be legitimate paid work reviewing home listings and is illegally branded with HomeNest's logo and colour palette.
consumers_across_canada_are_warned_to_av: Consumers across Canada are warned to avoid this prolific, highly convincing scam that HomeNest has been made aware of by concerned consumers, some of whom have been targeted. The scammers approach victims through various platforms, such as adding WhatsApp and Telegram users to the scam's chat groups, posting jobs on LinkedIn and Indeed to advertise the fake opportunity, cold calling and texting victims, and more.
each_path_takes_the_unsuspecting_consume: Each path takes the unsuspecting consumer to a scam website that illegally uses HomeNest's logo and branding, and claims to offer payment to analyze and promote the most profitable properties on a freelance basis. They may also use other similar methods that are designed to make victims send them funds.
image_screenshot_of_the_scam_website_hom: Image: Screenshot of the scam website home page falsely branded as HomeNest
like_many_such_scams_the_victims_are_ask: Like many such scams, the victims are asked to deposit funds into an account to get the job with the promise that this will be far outweighed by earnings. This is followed by the scammers demanding increasingly high deposits to keep their account active.
however_much_the_victim_pays_into_the_ac: However much the victim pays into the account, they will never see that money again and they will never be paid.
homenest_has_learned_of_at_least_one_use: HomeNest has learned of at least one user who believed the scam and has unfortunately lost thousands of dollars that they cannot recover, along with another who has lost hundreds.
the_scam_also_uses_homenest_s_branding_o: The scam also uses HomeNest's branding on letterhead to send official-looking, watermarked 'legal breach of contract' notices claiming the victim did not file their work within a certain period and demanding huge fines be paid.
homenest_has_received_a_copy_of_such_a_l: HomeNest has received a copy of such a letter from a scam victim who reached out to us. Much of the letter's text is extremely badly written and challenging to understand. What is clear is that the copy HomeNest received demands 87,140 USDT (Tether, a form of cryptocurrency) in payment, claiming that the fine will be refunded if the full amount is paid, and threatening legal action if it is not. See screenshot below.
image_screenshot_of_a_letter_sent_to_a_v: Image: Screenshot of a letter sent to a victim of the scam, falsely claiming to be from HomeNest
the_letter_is_signed_john_steen_project_: The letter is signed 'John Steen, Project Director, HomeNest' and marked with a convincing-looking stamp. No such employee or role exists at HomeNest Inc.
the_homenest_team_can_confirm_that_this_: The HomeNest team can confirm that this fraudulent scheme has no link of any kind to HomeNest Inc. or any of its associates, and that the company has no control over the scammers' illegal activity.
homenest_further_wishes_to_clarify_that_: HomeNest further wishes to clarify that it never makes job offers via WhatsApp or Telegram, nor does it pay users for clicking on listings or reviewing them.
michael_carney_homenest_s_director_of_bu: Michael Carney, HomeNest's Director of Business Development, said: 'We at HomeNest are appalled that scammers are hijacking the HomeNest brand to shake down prospective job-seekers. We're extremely concerned that people are losing money, and we want to sound the alarm to help prevent this from happening to anyone else.'
homenest_has_now_notified_the_appropriat: HomeNest has now notified the appropriate law enforcement agencies about the scam.
